R0287.title: AI Investment Agent Manipulation
R0287.definition: Attackers target AI investment advisers, research assistants, quant agents, or trading agents with prompt injection, data poisoning, model inversion, or synthetic market-signal inducement.
R0287.description:
AI investment agent manipulation is the financial-trading manifestation of general AI-agent risk. Attackers can hide malicious instructions in news, research reports, webpages, social content, trading comments, or data feeds to induce agents to ignore risk constraints, call privileged tools, output wrong investment advice, or execute wrong trades.

It also includes synthetic market signals, hallucination exploitation, agent poisoning, AI consensus attacks, model inversion, and data poisoning. Because investment agents may connect to market data, order routing, research, risk controls, and funding systems, manipulation can escalate from wrong text to real trades and financial loss.
R0287.influence: It distorts AI investment advice, causes erroneous automated trades, manipulates model consensus, leaks sensitive trading strategies, and causes financial loss.

references.title: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)

observables: External content used by agents contains hidden instructions or privileged-action inducement
Multiple agents output highly similar trading advice under the same forged signal
Agent tool calls exceed research-task boundaries and trigger orders, exports, or high-risk APIs
Poisoned training or retrieval sources cause systematic advice drift
